notes: Current registered control. Absence of a distinct pollinating anther is source-secure and the 2021 plastome tree places M. australasica sister to the sampled remainder of Monochoria. Direct species-level pollination evidence and exclusion of unsampled/alternatively sampled nonheterantherous congeners remain open.

PlantNET describes the six stamens as more or less equal, supporting absence of the case-defining heteranthery. M. cyanea is represented in the 2018 total-evidence phylogeny but absent from the 2021 plastome sample used for the incumbent-control receipt. Direct flower-visitation/pollination evidence and relative proximity to the case remain unresolved.
Current registered shared control. Heteranthery absence is source-secure; direct species-level pollination evidence and closest-eligible closure remain open.
Alternative equal-stamen congener that must be included in the closest-control search. Direct pollination evidence and relative phylogenetic proximity remain unresolved, so it is not promoted.
Retained as an auditable failed candidate. Luo et al. 2009 code long and short stamen sets and include S. surattensis among heteromorphic-stamen species.

Rejected after primary-morphology audit. Irwin and Barneby describe three long and four short fertile stamens with different anther dimensions. A later comparative table labelled the species non-heterantherous, but the frozen U3 definition follows the directly described discrete fertile-stamen sets.

The S. alata plastome study recovers S. siamea as a close relative, but morphology independently divides its seven fertile stamens into two long and five short sets; Luo et al. also code multiple stamen classes. Close phylogenetic proximity therefore cannot rescue the negative-control gate.

Irwin and Barneby describe seven fertile anthers as isomorphic, with abaxial anthers only sometimes slightly longer, so the frozen heteranthery-absence gate passes. Bee-resource records support floral use but do not yet close effective animal-pollination eligibility, and clade-level placement does not prove that this is the closest eligible control.
Retained as an auditable failed candidate. Weaker differentiation than the case does not establish heteranthery absence.
Rejected after primary-morphology audit. Three long and four short fertile stamens violate the frozen absence criterion even though a later synthesis called the species non-heterantherous.

A 2025 ITS analysis recovers S. corymbosa and S. bicapsularis as sister taxa, but direct floral work describes differentiated stamen functions/heteranthery. Sister status therefore increases phylogenetic quality but cannot override failure of the outcome-absence gate.

Irwin and Barneby describe the fertile stamens as not differentiated into two sets, supporting the frozen absence criterion. S. armata belongs to the adjacent VIIb architecture in the Senna phylogenetic framework, but exact closest-eligible placement and source-secure effective pollination remain unresolved.
